ch.s: Verses 1–10: “King Astyages was gathered to his fathers, and Cyrus the Persian received his kingdom.”; Verses 11–20: “So Bel’s priests said, “Behold, we will leave; but you, O king, set out the food, and mix the wine and set it out, shut the door securely…”; Verses 21–30: “and took the priests with their wives and children, who showed him the secret doors, where they came in and consumed the things that were on the table.”; Verses 31–40: “They cast him into the lion’s den, where he was six days.”; Verses 41–42: “Then the king cried with a loud voice, saying, “Great are you, O Lord, you God of Daniel, and there is none other beside you!””. People named: Daniel, Habakkuk, Cyrus, Jew, On. Places: Babylon.
q: Read verses 1–10. What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 11–20, what do you learn about leadership and kingship?
Read verse 4 slowly. What does it say about God, about people, and about how to live?
What does Daniel’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of worship and praise in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Bel and the Dragon?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.a: Write down three things this chapter shows about God and thank Him for each.
